children.translated_text: This group beginning with <s>dūrvā</s>, as well as the group beginning with <s>nyagrodha</s> that will be stated below, the group beginning with <s>padmaka</s>, <s>śāliparṇī</s> and <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, the lotus, whether water-born or wild <s>kuṭannaṭa</s>, and the group beginning with <s>sārivā</s>: these destroy <s>pitta</s>.
If there are <s>ma</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ga</s>, and <s>ga</s>, with the Vedas and worlds, it is <s>śālinī</s>.

children.text: āragvadhādyādayo gaṇāḥ saptaite balāsaṃ śleṣmāṇaṃ jayanti ||
children.translated_text: These seven groups, beginning with the <s>āragvadhādi</s> group, conquer <s>balāsa</s>, that is, <s>śleṣman</s>.
The group beginning with <s>jīvantī</s> is called life-promoting.
And this is merely an example.

children.text: dhīmatā svāduśītasnigdhādīn jīvantyādiṣu sādhāraṇaguṇān ālocya kṣīrekṣudrākṣākṣoḍavidārikandādiṣu tadguṇeṣu jīvanīyāditvam avadhārayituṃ yuktamiti ||
children.translated_text: A wise person, considering the common qualities among the <s>jīvantī</s> group, such as sweetness, coldness, and unctuousness, should determine life-promoting status and the like in milk, sugarcane, grapes, walnuts, <s>vidārīkanda</s>, and other things that possess those qualities.
<s>Jīvantī</s> is life-increasing.

children.text: kākolyau dve ekā kākolī kevaḍīsaṃjñā anyā kṣīrakākolī payasvinīsaṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>kākolī</s>s are these: one is <s>kākolī</s>, called <s>kevaḍī</s>; the other is <s>kṣīrakākolī</s>, called <s>payasvinī</s>.

children.text: dve mede ekā medā maṇicchidrāsaṃjñā anyā mahāmedā vṛkṣaruhāsaṃjñā ||
children.translated_text: The two <s>medā</s>s are these: one is <s>medā</s>, called <s>maṇicchidrā</s>; the other is <s>mahāmedā</s>, called <s>vṛkṣaruhā</s>.
The names of <s>mudgaparṇī</s> and the rest have been stated earlier.
In the half-verse of the <s>āryā</s>, with seven groups ending in two and beginning with an intermediate one, heavy, and with <s>sa</s>, <s>da</s>, <s>dha</s>, and <s>la</s>...

children.text: āryārdhe nātrāyuji jaḥ ṣaṣṭho'yaṃ nalaghukau vā ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the odd half, the sixth is <s>ja</s>, or <s>na</s> and two light syllables.

children.text: snehasya sarpirāder vidhiḥ snehavidhiḥ taṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rule for unctuous substance, beginning with ghee, is the <s>snehavidhi</s>; we shall explain it.
The rest should be supplied as before.

children.text: gurvādiguṇayuktaṃ yad dravyaṃ tat snehanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: A substance that possesses qualities such as heaviness is <s>snehana</s>, uncting.
What is opposite to this, endowed with the qualities of lightness, heat, stability, dryness, sharpness, grossness, hardness, and density, is drying.
The word 'mostly' should be construed with both drying and uncting.

children.text: tathā ca laghvapi sārṣapaṃ tailaṃ chāgaṃ ca dugdhaṃ tathā viṣkirapratudamṛgākhyaṃ vargatrayaṃ snehanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, even mustard oil, though light, and goat's milk, and the three classes called <s>viṣkira</s>, <s>pratuda</s>, and deer, are uncting.

children.text: tathā uṣṇam api matsyamahiṣamāṃsaṃ snehanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, fish and buffalo meat, though hot, are uncting.
The same should be understood also in the case of drying.

children.text: tathā ca yavo guruśītasarādiguṇayukto 'pi virūkṣaṇas tathā rājamāṣo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Thus barley, though endowed with qualities such as heaviness, coldness, and mobility, is drying, and so too <s>rājamāṣa</s>.

children.text: snehane prakṛte 'pi virūkṣaṇopanyāso 'nvayavyatirekeṇa sutarāṃ snehasya samyakpratipādanārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although uncting is the topic, drying is mentioned so that unctuous substance may be explained more completely by agreement and difference.

children.text: sneheṣu kṣīrānūpāmiṣādiṣu madhye sarpirādayaś catvāraḥ snehāḥ prakarṣeṇa varāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among unctuous substances such as milk and meat of marsh-dwelling animals, the four unctuous substances beginning with ghee are especially the best.

children.text: tatrāpi ca teṣv api caturṣu madhye sarpir uttamam saṃskārasyānuvartanāt ||
children.translated_text: And even among those, among those four, ghee is the highest, because it follows the preparation.

children.text: nanu yadi saṃskāram anuvartate sarpis tadānīṃ maricacitrakādidravyābhisaṃskṛtasya ghṛtasya śaityādiguṇāviparyāsaḥ prāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objection: if ghee follows the preparation, then, when ghee is processed with substances such as black pepper and <s>citraka</s>, a reversal of its qualities such as coldness would follow.
But this is not observed.

children.text: yad asya śaityādayo guṇā vinaśyantyauṣṇyādayaś cotpadyante iti ||
children.translated_text: That is, its qualities such as coldness do not perish and qualities such as heat do not arise.
To this it is said:
The prefix <s>anu</s> here has the sense of 'together with,' since particles have many meanings.

children.text: tenāyam arthaḥ sarpiṣo guṇāḥ saṃskāraguṇaiḥ saha vartante na tu tailādīnām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is the meaning: the qualities of ghee exist together with the qualities of the preparation, but this is not so for oils and the like.
For oil, fat, and marrow, under the influence of preparation, abandon their own qualities.

children.text: atra codāharaṇaṃ yathā candanādyaṃ tailam iti ||
children.translated_text: Here the example is sandalwood oil and the like.

children.text: ato dravyaguṇāntarair anabhibhūtaguṇatvāt sarpiṣa itareṣāṃ ca tailādīnāṃ dravyair abhibhūtaguṇatvād uttamatvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore ghee is superior because its qualities are not overwhelmed by the qualities of other substances, while the others, oil and the like, are inferior because their qualities are overwhelmed by other substances.

children.text: ata eva ca vātapittajvarādiṣu vikāreṣu ghṛtasādhyeṣu bheṣajaṃ tailaṃ neṣṭam aniṣṭasampādanāt ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in disorders such as fever caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> that are to be treated with ghee, medicinal oil is not desired, because it produces an undesirable result.

children.text: tailasādhyeṣu tu vikāreṣu tadupaśāntyarthaṃ tathāvidhadravyasaṃskṛtaṃ ghṛtam apīṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: But in disorders treatable by oil, ghee prepared with substances of that kind is also desired for the purpose of pacifying them.
For that is not so much a cause of what is undesirable.

children.text: tasmāt sarvasnehebhyaḥ sarpir evottamam saṃskārasyānuvartanād iti nyāyāt nyāyyam eva ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, on the principle that "among all unctuous substances ghee itself is best, because it follows the processing," this is quite proper.
And also because it is the cause of sweetness and the like.

children.text: yo yaḥ pūrvo yathāpūrvam yo ya uttaro yathottaram ||
children.translated_text: "Whichever is earlier, in order of earlierness; whichever is later, in order of laterness."
In the expression "according to similarity," this is an indeclinable compound.
The earlier is so in relation to the later, and the later is so in relation to the earlier.

children.text: tena caturṇāṃ snehānāṃ yathānirdiṣṭānāṃ sarpirādīnāṃ traya eva snehā vasāmajjasarpiḥsaṃjñakā yathāpūrvatvena sambadhyante na tu tailākhyaḥ snehaḥ tasya pūrvatvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, of the four unctuous substances, as specified, beginning with ghee, only three substances called fat, marrow, and ghee are connected with "in order of earlierness," but not the unctuous substance called oil, because it has no earlierness.

children.text: na hy anyo 'smāt kaścid uttaro 'sti yadapekṣyaiṣaḥ pūrvatvam ātmana āsādayet ||
children.translated_text: For there is no other substance later than this in relation to which it might acquire earlierness for itself.
Therefore oil has no relation of earlierness.

children.text: tathā caturṇāṃ snehānāṃ traya eva snehā majjavasātailākhyā yathottaratvenābhisaṃbadhyante na sarpiḥsaṃjñakaḥ snehaḥ uttaratvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, of the four unctuous substances, only the three substances called marrow, fat, and oil are connected with "in order of laterness," not the unctuous substance called ghee, because it has no laterness.

children.text: na hy anyaḥ kaścid asya pūrvo vidyate yad apekṣayaivottaratvam ātmana āsādayatīty uktam ||
children.translated_text: For, as has been said, there is no other substance earlier than it in relation to which it might acquire laterness for itself.
Thus, then, "in order of earlierness."
The property of counteracting <s>pitta</s> has been stated generally for fat, marrow, and ghee.

children.text: viśeṣeṇa ca vasā pittaghnī majjā pittaghnataraḥ sarpiḥ pittaghnatamam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In particular, the meaning is: fat counteracts <s>pitta</s>, marrow counteracts <s>pitta</s> more strongly, and ghee counteracts <s>pitta</s> most strongly.
"They counteract the others," and so on.

children.text: itarau vātakaphau pittāpekṣayā tau ghnanti parākurvantītītaraghnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The two others, namely <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> in relation to <s>pitta</s>, they destroy or overcome; therefore they are called "counteracting the others."
In order of laterness, the three unctuous substances called marrow, fat, and oil counteract <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>.

children.text: tena majjā vātaśleṣmaghno vasā vātaśleṣmaghnatarā tailaṃ vātaśleṣmaghnatamam ity avagantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus it should be understood that marrow counteracts <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, fat counteracts <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> more strongly, and oil counteracts <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> most strongly.

children.text: anye tv evaṃ vyācakṣate śleṣmaṇi snehaniṣedhād itaraghnā iti sāmānyoktāv api vātaghnā iti gamyate ||
children.translated_text: Others explain it thus: since unctuous treatment is prohibited in <s>śleṣman</s>, even though "counteracting the others" is stated generally, it is understood to mean "counteracting <s>vāta</s>."
Or else, in comparison with ghee and the other substances prepared with other drugs, <s>kapha</s> too is included by the word "other."

children.text: ghṛtād guruṇaḥ sakāśāt tailaṃ guru gurutaram ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oil is heavy in comparison with ghee, which is heavy; the meaning is that it is heavier.
But fat is the heaviest in comparison with oil.
And marrow is heaviest to an even greater degree than that.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ snehābhyāṃ sarpirvasābhyāṃ sarpistailābhyāṃ sarpirmajjabhyām dvābhyāṃ ityādi dvābhyāṃ yamako nāmnā snehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With two unctuous substances, ghee and fat, ghee and oil, or ghee and marrow, and so on, the unctuous substance called <s>yamaka</s> is made from two.

children.text: evaṃ tribhiḥ snehais trivṛtaḥ caturbhir ucyate mahāsnehaḥ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, with three unctuous substances it is called <s>trivṛt</s>; with four, the remainder is to be supplied: it is called <s>mahāsneha</s>.
"Beginning with those to be oleated": those who are to be oleated are those fit for oleation.
The meaning is that one who has not been oleated is not fit to be fomented.

children.text: evaṃ yo'pi śodhyaḥ so 'pi pūrvaṃ snehyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, one who is to be purified too must first be oleated.
Those to be fomented are those fit for fomentation.
Here the suffix <s>ṇya</s>, a <s>kṛtya</s> suffix, has the sense of fitness.

children.text: evaṃ saṃśodhyāḥ śodhanārhāḥ stryāsaktā madyāsaktāḥ tathā vyāyāmasaktāś ca tathā cintakāḥ tathā vṛddhā bālā abalā alpabalāḥ kṛśā rūkṣāḥ kṣīṇarudhirāḥ kṣīṇaśukrāśca vātārtāḥ vātapīḍitāḥ syandādiṣu pratyekasmin yojyaḥ syandinaḥ akṣirogayuktāḥ timiriṇaś ca dāruṇapratibodhinaḥ kṛcchronmīlinaḥ snehārhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, those to be purified are those fit for purification: those attached to women, those addicted to liquor, those devoted to exercise, those given to worry, the old, children, the weak, those of slight strength, the emaciated, the dry, those whose blood is depleted, those whose semen is depleted, and those afflicted by <s>vāta</s>, that is, oppressed by <s>vāta</s>. The word is to be applied separately to each of <s>syanda</s> and the rest: those with eye diseases such as <s>syanda</s>, those with <s>timira</s>, and those who awaken with difficulty, that is, who open their eyes with difficulty, are fit for oleation.
Those beginning with excessively weak digestive fire are not to be oleated.
The word "excessively" is to be construed separately as far as "the weak."
Thus the meaning is that the excessively weak are not to be oleated.

children.text: ata evālpabalāḥ snehyāḥ na tv atidurbalāḥ iti na pūrvāparāvirodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, those of slight strength are to be oleated, but not the excessively weak; so there is no contradiction between the earlier and later statements.
In one whose digestive fire is excessively sharp, oleation causes an excessive increase of fire.
And in one who is excessively stout, it causes increase of digestive fire and fat.
And in one who is excessively weak, because of inability to digest, there is disorder from the unctuous substance.

children.text: ūrustambhādibhir yāvanmadyaiś ca pīḍitā na snehyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by <s>ūrustambha</s> and the like, and as far as those afflicted by liquors, are not to be oleated.
"A woman who has recently miscarried," that is, whose embryo has been discharged, is not to be oleated; here there is a change of gender and number.

children.text: prayukte ca nasyādikarmaṇi sarva eva na snehyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when procedures such as nasal therapy have been administered, none of them at all are to be oleated.

children.text: tatra teṣu sneheṣu madhye dhīsmṛtyādyabhilāṣiṇāṃ ghṛtaṃ śasyate yāvad agnikāṅkṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: Among those unctuous substances, ghee is recommended for those desiring intellect, memory, and the like, down to those desiring digestive fire.
Others read: "for those desiring intelligence and the like."
By the word "and the like," voice, lifespan, complexion, and so on are included.
Oil is recommended in those suffering from glandular swellings and the like.
It is recommended for persons desiring lightness and firmness, and for those with a hard bowel.
<s>Vāta</s> and the others are to be connected separately with depleted tissues.

children.text: vātakṣīṇadhātuṣu evam ātapakṣīṇadhātuṣv ityādi śeṣau ghṛtatailābhyām uktābhyām anyau vasāmajjānau śasyete ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in those whose tissues are depleted by <s>vāta</s>, and similarly in those whose tissues are depleted by heat and the like, the remaining two, fat and marrow, distinct from the previously mentioned ghee and oil, are recommended.
Likewise in those who are dry and so on, and similarly in those able to endure hardship.

children.text: atyagniṣu mahāgniṣu balavadagniṣv iti draṣṭavyam anyathātyagniṣu snehaniṣedhāt pūrvāparavirodhaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "in those with excessive fire," it should be understood as "in those with great fire, with strong digestive fire"; otherwise there would be a contradiction with the earlier prohibition of oleation in those with excessive fire.

children.text: athavā atyagniṣv api vasāmajjānāv anujajñe apavādavākyatvād asyeti vyākhyeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or else it should be explained that even in those with excessive fire he allows fat and marrow, because this is an exceptional statement.

children.text: vātenāvṛtāḥ panthānaḥ chidrākhyāḥ yeṣāṃ teṣu ca śasyete śeṣau ||
children.translated_text: And in those whose pathways, called openings, are obstructed by <s>vāta</s>, the remaining two are recommended.
The particle <s>tu</s> marks distinction.
The particle <s>ca</s> marks conjunction.
The word "pain" is to be connected separately with each item.
That is, "in joint pains, in bone pains," and so on.

children.text: tathā dagdharujy āhataruji ca tathā bhraṣṭayonirujīty evaṃ sambandhaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the connection should be made as: 'in pain from burning,' 'in pain from injury,' and likewise 'in pain from a displaced womb.'
The connection is: oil is recommended in the rainy season.
The same construction should also be applied in what follows.

children.text: svasthasya snehanārthaṃ sarvasyaiva snehasya prasaṅge niyamo 'yaṃ kriyate tailaṃ prāvṛṣy eva varṣānte eva sarpiḥ anyau vasāmajjānau mādhava eveti ||
children.translated_text: When the topic is any unctuous substance for the oleation of a healthy person, this restriction is made: oil only in the rainy season, ghee only at the end of the rains, and the other two, fat and marrow, only in spring.

children.text: sādhāraṇe ṛtau śrāvaṇādau saṃśodhanāt pūrvaṃ snehanārthaṃ snehaḥ sarpirādiś catuṣprakāro 'pi śastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In an ordinary season, beginning with Śrāvaṇa, before purification therapy, all four kinds of unctuous substance, ghee and the rest, are recommended for oleation.
Likewise, by day, that is, in the daytime, not at night.
And when the sun is clear, its harsh rays not covered by clouds, mist, and the like.

children.text: sneha iti sāmānyaśabdaprayogāt sarvaḥ snehaḥ sarpirādiś catuṣprakāro gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: Because the general word 'sneha' is used, every unctuous substance is understood: the fourfold kind beginning with ghee.

children.text: tvarāyāṃ satyāṃ vyādhikriyāṃ prati prāpte kāle snehayogyatāyāṃ satyām śīte hemantaśiśirākhye kāle tailaṃ saṃśodhanāt pūrvaṃ snehanārthaṃ śastam nānyaḥ snehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is urgency, when the time for treating the disease has arrived, and when the patient is fit for oleation, in the cold season called hemanta and śiśira, oil is recommended before purification therapy for the sake of oleation, and no other unctuous substance.

children.text: apiśabdān na kevalaṃ varṣāsu avarṣāsu ca śastam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the word 'also' the meaning is that it is recommended not only during the rains but also outside the rains.

children.text: na kevalaṃ śaradi ghṛtaṃ prayuñjīta yāvad gharme 'pi ghṛtaṃ niśy upayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: One should use ghee not only in autumn; rather, in the hot season too one should take ghee at night.

children.text: na ca gharma eva niśy upayuñjīta yāvat pitte kupite tajje vā vikāre tathā pavane kupite tajje vā vikāre snehasādhye gharme ghṛtaṃ niśy upayuñjīta na divā na ca tailaṃ vasāmajjānau vā ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one take it at night only in the hot season; rather, when pitta is aggravated, or in a disorder arising from it, and likewise when wind is aggravated, or in a disorder arising from it, if the condition is curable by sneha, one should take ghee at night in the hot season, not by day, and not oil, fat, or marrow.

children.text: tathā pittavati pittādhike saṃsarge vātapittākhye śleṣmapittākhye kupite tajje vā vikāre snehasādhye gharme ghṛtam eva niśy upayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in a pitta-dominant combined condition, namely when vāta-pitta or śleṣman-pitta is aggravated, or in a disorder arising from it and curable by sneha, one should use only ghee at night in the hot season.

children.text: pitte pavana ity etat doṣavikārobhayopalakṣaṇārthaṃ vedyam ||
children.translated_text: The words 'in pitta' and 'in wind' should be understood as indicating both the doṣa and its disorder.
In 'pittavati,' the possessive suffix matup is used in the sense of abundance.
'Otherwise' means by a method different from the one stated.

children.text: yathā śītakāle niśi ghṛtopayogāt vātakaphāddheto rogā bhaveyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For example, from using ghee at night in the cold season, diseases could arise from vāta and kapha.

children.text: tathā divā gharme kāle tailopayogāt pittataḥ pittāt rogāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, from using oil by day in the hot season, diseases could arise from pitta.

children.text: vasāmajjños tv aniścitasvarūpatvāt na tūṣṇakāle nāpi śītakāle tvarāyāṃ satyām upayogas tantrakāreṇa darśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But because the nature of fat and marrow is indeterminate, their use when there is urgency is not taught by the author of the treatise either in the hot season or in the cold season.

children.text: tathā coktam yathāsattvaṃ tu śaityoṣṇe vasāmajjños tu nirdiśet iti ||
children.translated_text: And it has been said accordingly: 'One should prescribe fat and marrow according to their actual coldness or heat.'
Yukti is yoga, in the sense of a method or means.

children.text: yuktyā mātrākālakriyābhūmidehadoṣasvabhāvayā snehaṃ sarpirādikam avacārayet upayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: By proper method, with regard to dose, time, procedure, region, body, doṣa, and constitution, one should administer, that is, use, an unctuous substance such as ghee.
He states with what it is to be taken: with food beginning with chewables.
By the word 'and so on' are included all three kinds of food: what is eaten, licked, and drunk.
Likewise, one should administer sneha by enemas, nasal therapy, massage, and gargling.
The word tarpaṇa is to be connected separately with the head and the others.
Thus, by tarpaṇa of the head, called śirobasti.
Likewise, by tarpaṇa of the ears, called filling the ears.
Likewise, by tarpaṇa of the eyes, taught in the procedure for tarpaṇa and puṭapāka.
'Chewable' means such things as śaśāṅkakiraṇa; with that chewable food.
By the inclusion of 'and so on,' rice and the other items taught by the sage are understood.
And accordingly the sage says:

children.text: odanaśca vilepī ca raso māṃsaṃ payo dadhi
children.translated_text: Cooked rice, thick gruel, soup, meat, milk, curds,

children.text: yavāgūḥ sūpaśāke ca yūṣaḥ kāmbalikaḥ khalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thin gruel, pulses and vegetables, yūṣa, kāmbalika, and khala;
saktu, enema, ground preparations, liquor, and likewise linctuses,
chewable food, massage, enema, and also the upper enemas.
Thus.
The plural expression 'by enemas' is meant to include the three kinds of enema.
Accordingly, these are nirūha, anvāsana, and uttara enema.

children.text: rasabhedaścaikakatvaṃ ca tābhyāṃ rasabhedaikakatvābhyāṃ snehasyāvacāryamāṇasya catuḥṣaṣṭir vicāraṇā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By difference of taste and by being single, that is, through difference of taste and single use, the unctuous substance being administered has sixty-four modes of preparation.

children.text: rasabhedena ṣaṭ pañcakāḥ ṣaṭ ca pṛthak ityādigranthanirdiṣṭena triṣaṣṭisaṅkhyāvacchinnena sahopayuktasya snehasya tathaikakatvena asahāyena kevalena snehena satāsya snehasya catuḥṣaṣṭirvicāraṇāḥ snehaprayogakalpanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When an unctuous substance is used together with the set delimited by the number sixty-three, described in the textual passage beginning 'six pentads by difference of taste and six separately,' and also when it is single, that is, with an unassisted and plain sneha, this sneha has sixty-four vicāraṇās, preparations for the application of sneha.

children.text: yā etā bhakṣyādyannena tathā rasabhedena mūrdhakarṇākṣitarpaṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: These are the ones with food beginning with chewables, with differences of taste, and with tarpaṇa of the head, ears, and eyes.

children.text: yā etāḥ kramāt yathākramaṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ tāḥ kalpanāḥ snehasyānyābhibhūtatvāt anyena bhakṣyādinā bahunā tathā rasabhedena sahopayuktasyābhibhūtatvāt tathālpatvād alpopayogitvāt mūrdhākṣitarpaṇādau hi pāna iva prabhūtasyāvacārayitum aśakyatvācca vicāraṇāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These preparations that have been listed in order are remembered as vicāraṇās because the sneha is overpowered by something else: when it is used with many other things such as chewable foods, and with differences of taste, it is overpowered; and because of smallness, that is, because only a small amount is used, since in tarpaṇa of the head and eyes and the like it is impossible to administer a large amount as in drinking.
The remainder to be supplied is: by the authors of Ayurveda.
This is the reason, as stated, for plain sneha having the name vicāraṇā.

children.text: tasya yathoktasya hetorabhāvād avidyamānatvāt yo'cchapeyasnehaḥ kevala eva na saṃyuktaḥ nāsau vicāraṇā kevalopayogitvād bahūpayogitvāccetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because that stated reason is absent, because it does not exist, the sneha that is to be drunk plain, being simply alone and not combined, is not a vicāraṇā, since it is used alone and used in large quantity; this is the meaning.

children.text: nanu iha kevalaḥ sneho na vicāraṇetyucyate ||
children.translated_text: But one may object: here plain sneha is said not to be a vicāraṇā.
Earlier, however, the use of plain sneha itself in enema and the like was called a vicāraṇā.
We think that this seems to contradict what comes before and after.
This is not so.

children.text: acchapeya ityasya hyayamarthaḥ acchaḥ kevalo yaḥ snehaḥ pīyate sā vicāraṇā na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For the meaning of "plain drinking" is this: when a clear, unmixed sneha is drunk, that is not a vicāraṇā.

children.text: mūrdhāditarpaṇādinā tu kevalasya snehasya ya upayogaḥ sā vicāraṇeti ||
children.translated_text: But the use of unmixed sneha by tarpaṇa of the head and the like is a vicāraṇā.

children.text: acchapeyākhyaḥ kalpaḥ prayogaḥ snehasya śreṣṭhaḥ praśasyatamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The procedure called plain drinking is the best, the most praised, application of sneha.

children.text: kutaḥ ityāha snehakarmāśusādhanāt snehakarmaṇāṃ tarpaṇamārdavādīnāṃ śīghraṃ sampādanāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? He states the reason: because it quickly accomplishes the action of sneha, since it rapidly produces the actions of sneha, such as nourishment and softness.

children.text: dvābhyāṃ yāmābhyāṃ praharābhyāṃ yā snehasya mātrā prayuktā jāṭharānalavaśājjarāṃ yāti sā tasya hrasvā mātrā caturbhir yāmairyā jīryati sā tasya madhyamā mātrā aṣṭābhir yāmair yā jīryati sottamā mātrā kramāt yathākramaṃ tā hrasvamadhyamottamā mātrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The dose of sneha which, when administered, is digested by the force of the gastric fire in two yāmas, that is, two praharas, is its small dose; the one that is digested in four yāmas is its medium dose; and the one that is digested in eight yāmas is the highest dose. In order, these are the small, medium, and highest doses.

children.text: tābhyaścatisṛbhyo mātrābhyo hrasīyasā atiśayena hrasvāṃ mātrāṃ kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: From those three doses one should formulate an even smaller dose, one that is extremely small.
The word to be supplied is "the physician."

children.text: hrasvamadhyottamā iti nirdeśe ḍyāpoḥ ityādinā hrasvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the expression "small, medium, and highest," the shortening is by the rule beginning "ḍyāpoḥ."

children.text: hrasvā mātrā yāmadvayajaraṇalakṣaṇā uktā tato'pyarvākkālena yā jarāṃ yāti sā hrasīyasīti ||
children.translated_text: The small dose has been stated as characterized by digestion in two yāmas; a dose that is digested in a time even earlier than that is called the smaller one.

children.text: doṣādīn doṣabheṣajadeśakālabalaśarīrāhārasattvasātmyaprakṛtīḥ vīkṣya ākalayya prāk pūrvameva ajñātakoṣṭhe puruṣa uttamamātrāviṣaye pūrvaṃ hrasīyasīṃ kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having observed and estimated the doṣas and the rest, namely the doṣa, medicine, region, time, strength, body, diet, mental constitution, habituation, and prakṛti, in a person whose bowel nature is unknown, the physician should first formulate the smaller dose before dealing with the case suitable for the highest dose.

children.text: tato hrasvāṃ tato madhyamāṃ tata uttamāṃ ca prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: After that he should formulate the small dose, then the medium dose, and then the highest dose.

children.text: evaṃ madhyamamātrāṃ viṣaye hrasīyasīṃ hrasvamātrāviṣaye'pi hrasīyasīṃ prākkalpayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the case suitable for the medium dose too, he should first formulate the smaller dose; and even in the case suitable for the small dose, he should first formulate the smaller dose.
Otherwise there would be danger of adverse consequence.
The particle eva has the sense of restriction.
The word tu is meant to indicate sequence in the phrase "each later one."
It is also said in the Saṅgraha: "In a person whose bowel nature is unknown, a large dose would create danger to life."
Thus.

children.text: iyaṃ hrasvā iyaṃ hrasvā iyamanayoratiśayena hrasvā iti hrasīyasī ||
children.translated_text: "This is small, this is smaller, and this is extremely smaller than those two"; so it is called hrasīyasī, "the smaller one."
In the word hrasīyasī, when the suffix īyasun is added, the loss of va occurs by the rule beginning "sthūladūra."
Others, however, state doses limited by the quantities of two palas, four palas, and six palas.
But this is not acceptable.
For doses of sneha administered without regard for the strength of the gastric fire lead only to harm.
Therefore we have not stated doses limited by quantities such as two palas.
Nor is this the view of the sage.
For his text is:
"It waits for a full day and night, a whole day,

children.text: pradhānā madhyamā hrasvā snehamātrā jarāṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: and half a day, with respect to digestion: the chief, medium, and small doses of sneha."
Thus.

children.text: hyastane'nne āhāre jīrṇa eva jīrṇamātra eva na tvannābhilāṣe sati śuddhaye śodhanārthaṃ bahuḥ uttamayā mātrayā sneho'cchaḥ kevalaḥ peyatvena śasyate ||
children.translated_text: Only when yesterday's food, the meal, has been digested, indeed just when it has become digested, but not when there is desire for food, is a large quantity of clear, unmixed sneha, in the highest dose, recommended to be drunk for purification, that is, for the purpose of cleansing therapy.

children.text: saṃjātabubhukṣeṇa tu pīto jāṭharānalasya dīptatvācchodhanakāryam akurvāṇas tadyogyatāṃ cānutpādayannāśveva jarāmupaiti ||
children.translated_text: But when it is drunk by one whose hunger has arisen, because the gastric fire is bright, it very quickly reaches digestion without performing the work of purification and without producing fitness for that work.

children.text: vamanamapi bubhukṣitasya na sampadyate kaphāpaciteḥ pūrvoktācca hetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Vomiting too is not successfully produced in a hungry person, because kapha has been diminished and for the reason stated earlier.
Therefore the statement, "only when yesterday's food has been digested," is properly stated.

children.text: śamano yo rogasya śamanāyopayujyate snehaḥ sa kṣudvato jātabubhukṣasya śasyate jātāyāṃ bubhukṣāyāṃ na jīrṇamātra evānne śodhana iva ||
children.translated_text: The pacifying sneha, the sneha that is used for pacifying a disease, is recommended for one who is hungry, whose desire to eat has arisen; it is used when hunger has arisen, not merely when the food has just been digested, as in purification therapy.

children.text: śamano hi sneho yatratatrasthaṃ doṣaṃ kupitaṃ sarvaśarīravyāpitvācchamanarūpatvāt ca śamayati ||
children.translated_text: For pacifying sneha pacifies the aggravated doṣa wherever it is situated, because it pervades the whole body and because it has the nature of pacification.

children.text: yadi punarjīrṇamātra evānne sneho'yamabubhukṣitasyaivopayujyate tadānīṃ srotasāṃ kaphādyupalepānivartanāt tatsaṃpṛktaḥ sa sneho na sarvaṃ śarīraṃ vyāpnute avyāpnuvaṃśca doṣaṃ na śamayet ||
children.translated_text: But if this sneha is used just when the food has been digested, by one who is not yet hungry, then, because the coating of the channels by kapha and the like has not been removed, that sneha, being mixed with them, does not pervade the whole body; and not pervading it, it would not pacify the doṣa.
Therefore this is recommended only for one who is hungry.

children.text: sa ca madhyamamātrayā anannaḥ kevala eva bhakṣyādināhāreṇa rahitaḥ accha eva peya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this, in a medium dose, is to be drunk without food, entirely by itself, free from food such as chewables; that is, it is to be drunk plain.

children.text: atra cottamayā mātrayā snehapānadinānantaraṃ pathyaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Here, when sneha is drunk in the highest dose, the regimen should be followed on the day after the sneha-drinking.
Then there is another application of sneha.
Again, on another day, the regimen should be followed.

children.text: madhyamamātrayā snehapāne tu laghubhojino yāmamātre'nnākāṅkṣā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: But when sneha is drunk in a medium dose, a light eater develops a desire for food after only one yāma.

children.text: tadā ca snehopayoge rātryārambhe rātriyāmārdhe gate vā rasakaudanaprāyaṃ bhojanaṃ bhojyaṃ mātrayaiva ||
children.translated_text: At that time, when the sneha is used at the beginning of the night or after half a night-yāma has passed, a meal consisting chiefly of meat broth and rice should be eaten, and only in proper measure.
For in the case of pacifying sneha the author of the treatise allowed only a small meal.

children.text: vakṣyati hi upacārastu śamane kāryaḥ snehe viriktavat ||
children.translated_text: For he will say: "In pacifying sneha, the regimen should be carried out as for one who has been purged."
Thus.
Nourishing sneha is recommended together with meat broth, liquor, and the like.
When rasa is mentioned without qualification, it should be known as the broth produced from meat.
According to the statement of another tantra, therefore, by the word rasa here one should understand meat broth.
By the word "and the like" there is inclusion of liquid substances such as milk and khaṇḍa.

children.text: tathā saha bhaktena odanādinā vartate iti sabhaktaśca śasyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because it is accompanied by food such as cooked rice, it is also recommended as sabhakta, "with food."
And this sneha is small, smaller even than the smaller dose.
This sneha is beneficial for children and the like.
The expression "children and the like" is an itaretara-dvandva compound.
Those who are afflicted by thirst are those oppressed by thirst.
Those who hate sneha are those who, by their very nature, dislike unctuous substances.
The word 'regular' is connected with both women and sneha: the meaning is, in those for whom women are regular and in those for whom sneha is regular.

children.text: kāle coṣṇe grīṣmādau kṛśeṣu ca nareṣu hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And it is beneficial in a hot season, beginning with summer, and for lean persons.

children.text: prāk ca madhyaṃ cottaraṃ ca prāṅmadhyottaram ||
children.translated_text: Before, middle, and after: this is 'before-middle-after.'
The sneha in which food is before, in the middle, or after is so called.

children.text: tenāyamarthaḥ bhaktasyādāvupayukto'sau sneho'dhodehajān vyādhīn jayet madhya upayukto madhyadehajān bhaktasyoparyupayukta ūrdhvadehajāniti yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is the meaning: that sneha, when used at the beginning of a meal, conquers diseases arising in the lower body; when used in the middle, diseases arising in the middle body; and when used after the meal, diseases arising in the upper body, respectively.

children.text: tathā aṅgānāṃ śarīrāvayavānām adhomadhyordhvasaṃjñakānāṃ balaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, it gives strength to the limbs, the bodily parts designated as lower, middle, and upper.
And this has been said:
When <s>māruta</s> is excessive, ghee with salt is always beneficial;

children.text: kevalaṃ tvadhike pitte kaphe satryūṣaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: but when pitta is excessive, it should be plain, and when kapha is excessive, it should likewise be with the three pungents.
Thus.
He obtains long life and the rest from rasāyana.
Why are these obtained from rasāyana? He answers: because it is the means of obtaining them.

children.text: yasmāt śreṣṭhānāṃ rasarudhirādīnāṃ yo lābhopāyaḥ sa rasāyanamucyate ||
children.translated_text: Since the means of obtaining the best rasa, blood, and so on is called rasāyana.

children.text: tad rasāyanaṃ jitātmanaḥ puruṣasyādye vayasi atibālyātikrāntamātre athavā madhyame vayasi prayojyam ||
children.translated_text: That rasāyana is to be employed for a self-controlled man in the first age of life, just after excessive childhood has passed, or in middle age.
For what sort of man? He says: one endowed with unctuousness and so on.

children.text: snigdhādiguṇayuktasya tathā sarvathā adha upariṣṭācca śuddhasya ||
children.translated_text: One endowed with qualities such as unctuousness, and likewise purified in every way both below and above.

children.text: yasmād aviśuddhe śarīre rāsāyano vidhir upayukto vājīkaro vopayukto niṣphalaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For when the body is impure, a rasāyana procedure that has been used, or an aphrodisiac procedure that has been used, would be fruitless.
As dye is fruitless on a dirty cloth.
For a dirty cloth does not take color.
The sages know the application of rasāyanas to be of two kinds.
Among them, the principal one is accomplished by entering a hut.
The vātātapika method is otherwise, that is, non-principal.

children.text: kva tatkurvīta pure prāpyopakaraṇīye harmyaṃ dhavalagṛhaṃ nivātaṃ nirbhayaṃ ca yasmintasmin tathodīcyāṃ diśi śubhe durbhikṣamarakādirahite kuṭīṃ trigarbhāṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Where should one perform it? In a city where the necessary equipment can be obtained, one should have built, in a mansion or white house that is windless and safe, and in the auspicious northern direction, free from famine, plague, and the like, a three-chambered hut.

children.text: prathamamekaṃ gṛham tasyābhyantare dvitīyam tasyābhyantare tṛtīyam evaṃ trigarbhā ||
children.translated_text: First there is one room; inside it a second; inside that a third: thus it is three-chambered.

children.text: trayo garbhāḥ antarāṇi yasyā iti kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: It is so called because it has three chambers, that is, inner spaces.
Likewise, it should have small windows.
Likewise, it should not be penetrated or invaded by smoke and the like.

children.text: tathā praguṇāni vaidyopakaraṇāni bheṣajādīni yasyāṃ tāṃ tathāvidhām ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, it should be such as has excellent medical equipment, medicines and the like.
It should be well cleansed, purified by smearing and the other procedures.

children.text: atha kṛtamaṅgalaḥ śubhe divase śuciḥ pūjyān gurumitrādīn sampūjya tāṃ pūrvopavarṇitāṃ kuṭīṃ praviśet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having performed auspicious rites on an auspicious day, being pure, and having honored venerable people, teachers, friends, and others, he should enter that hut described earlier.
Having established himself in that hut, he is purified by cleansing procedures.
He is comfortable and free from disease.
And this has been stated in a general way.
For such things as śilājatu and cyavanaprāśa are permitted even in diseases.

children.text: tathā ca vakṣyati na so 'sti rogo bhuvi sādhyarūpo jatvaśmajaṃ yaṃ na jayet prasahya ||
children.translated_text: And accordingly he will say: 'There is no curable disease on earth that the mountain-born bitumen does not forcibly overcome.'
Thus.

children.text: tathā ityeṣa cyavanaprāśo yaṃ prāśya cyavano muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise: 'This is <s>Cyavanaprāśa</s>, by consuming which the sage <s>Cyavana</s>,
even though worn out by old age, became a delight to the eyes of women.

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ kṣayaṃ śophaṃ vaisvaryaṃ ca vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: It removes cough, dyspnea, wasting, swelling, and hoarseness.'
Thus.

children.text: punarjātabala iti prakṛtibalena yo balavānnāsīttasya saṃśodhanena balahīnatvena punarjātabalo bṛṃhaṇāhārādīnāṃ yadā sa tadā rasāyanam ārabhetetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With restored strength' means this: when one who was not strong by natural strength has, after purificatory treatment and after weakness, regained strength through nourishing food and the like, then he should begin rasāyana.

children.text: asaṃjātabalo hy utkṛṣṭavīryāṇāṃ rasāyanānāṃ vīryaṃ soḍhuṃ na kṣamata iti punarjātabala ityuktam ||
children.translated_text: For one whose strength has not arisen cannot bear the potency of rasāyanas of intense power; therefore it is said, 'with restored strength.'
The term brahmacārī is stated with special reference to abstention from intercourse with women.
Likewise, he is one whose contentment has arisen.
He is faithful and free from greed.
Likewise, he delights in giving and is devoted to compassion and the like.
Likewise, he is devoted to the deities.
He is such that sleep and waking are properly regulated.
Likewise, he has affection for medicines and speaks pleasantly.

children.text: evaṃvidhena viśeṣaṇakalāpena yuktasya kāyavāṅmanoviśuddhasya rasāyane ca yatpūrvaṃ karaṇīyaṃ tadāha ||
children.translated_text: For a man endowed with this collection of qualifications, pure in body, speech, and mind, he now states what is to be done first in rasāyana.

children.text: harītakyādikaṃ yogam uṣṇajalena prāk snigdhasvinno naraḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: A man who has first been oleated and sweated should drink the preparation beginning with harītakī with hot water.
By that preparation he is properly purged.

children.text: anantaraṃ śuddhadehāya kṛtapeyādikakramāya ca trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ vā saptāhaṃ vā sarpiryutaṃ yāvakaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, for one whose body has been purified and who has completed the sequence beginning with thin gruel, one should give yāvaka mixed with ghee for three nights, five nights, or a week.

children.text: athavā purāṇaśakṛtaḥ śuddhiṃ yāvat tāvad yāvakaṃ sasarpiṣkaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or else one should give yāvaka with ghee until the old fecal matter is cleared.

children.text: trividhamalāpekṣayā trividhaṃ parijñānam hīnapurīṣasya trirātram madhyapurīṣasya pañcarātram utkṛṣṭapurīṣasya saptarātram iti ||
children.translated_text: There is threefold determination according to the threefold fecal matter: three nights for one with little stool, five nights for one with moderate stool, and seven nights for one with abundant stool.

children.text: tathā hi madhyabahuvarcaskasya pañcarātreṇa saptarātreṇa vā malaḥ śudhyati alpamalasya trirātreṇaiva iti trividhaṃ parijñānaṃ yuktam ||
children.translated_text: For one with a moderate or large amount of feces, the impurity is cleared in five nights or seven nights, while for one with little impurity it is cleared in three nights only; thus the threefold determination is appropriate.

children.text: bahutaramalasya bahutarairevāhobhiḥ śuddhiḥ syād ityuktavān ā śuddheḥ purāṇaśakṛto 'thavā iti ||
children.translated_text: For one with a very large amount of impurity, purification would occur only after a greater number of days; therefore he said, 'or until the old fecal matter is cleared.'

children.text: evaṃ saṃskṛtakoṣṭhasya narasya yasya yadrasāyanaṃ yaugikam upalabhyate sātmyajño bhiṣak sarvamālocya tasya tadrasāyanam upāharet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for a person whose digestive tract has been properly prepared, whatever compound <s>rasāyana</s> is found suitable for him, the physician who knows what is wholesome should consider everything and administer that <s>rasāyana</s> to him.
Because she removes all diseases, she is called <s>harītakī</s>.
Because she is wholesome for all the bodily constituents, she is <s>pathyā</s>; because she is auspicious, she is <s>śivā</s>.

children.text: yasmād vijayate vyādhīn samagrān vijayā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Because she conquers all diseases completely, therefore she is <s>vijayā</s>.
Freedom from all diseases arises, and life becomes enduring.
Because those who habitually use her gain fearlessness, therefore she is remembered as <s>abhayā</s>.

children.text: navā vṛttā ghanā snigdhā gurvī majjati cāpsu yā ||
children.translated_text: A fresh fruit, round, solid, unctuous, heavy, and one that sinks in water,
should be used for a child together with fresh butter.
In vāta it is recommended with ghee and salt; in pitta, with jaggery and sugar;
in kapha, with long pepper and honey; it is praised at all times.
Thus from the Elder <s>Vāgbhaṭa</s>.
One thousand <s>abhayā</s> fruits, combined with three thousand <s>āmalaka</s> fruits.

children.text: tathā pañcānāṃ pañcamūlānāṃ palaśatadvayaṃ sārdhaṃ salile daśaguṇe paktvā daśāṃśasthite rasa āpothya mṛditvā harītakyāmalakāni vyasthīni kṛtvā tasmin kvāthe prakṣipya kuḍavapramāṇaṃ tvagelādikaṃ cūrṇitaṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, two and a half hundred palas of the five kinds of <s>pañcamūla</s> should be boiled in ten times as much water. When one tenth remains as decoction, the <s>harītakī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> fruits should be crushed, rubbed, and freed from their stones, placed in that decoction, and a kuḍava measure of powdered bark, cardamom, and the rest should be added.
Gold and <s>nāgakeśara</s>.
'Freed from their stones' is neuter; by the rule 'when a neuter and a non-neuter remain together,' there is single remainder.

children.text: palaśatenādhikaṃ śarkarāyā ardhabhāram ghṛtasya trīṇy āḍhakāni dve cāḍhake tailāt tatsarvaṃ vahnau pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should cook all that on the fire with one hundred palas more of sugar, half a bhāra of ghee, three āḍhakas, and two āḍhakas of oil.

children.text: tacca lehatāṃ gatamavatīrṇaṃ śītaṃ kṣaudraśatais tribhir viṃśatyadhikair yuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: When it has reached the state of a linctus, has been taken down from the fire, and is cool, one should combine it with three hundred and twenty measures of honey.

children.text: viṃśairiti viṃśateḥ pūraṇe iti pūraṇe 'rthe ḍibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the word 'twenty,' in the sense of completing twenty, the suffix ḍi is used in the sense of completion.
By the rule 'for viṃśati there is ḍit,' with elision of ṭi, the word <s>viṃśa</s> is formed.
Afterwards, when it has been stirred with a churner, one should place it in a ghee vessel.

children.text: yā mātrā ekamāhāraṃ sāyantanaṃ noparundhyāt sāsya rasāyanasya mātrā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: That dose which does not obstruct the evening meal is remembered as the dose of this <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: āhāramekam iti vacanācca prathamāhārakālasya rasāyanamātrayāvaśyamuparodhaḥ kārya iti vedayati ||
children.translated_text: And by the expression 'one meal' it indicates that obstruction of the first meal time by the dose of <s>rasāyana</s> must necessarily be made.

children.text: asmiṃśca lehe jīrṇe ṣaṣṭikaḥ kṣīreṇa saha bhojanam iṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: When this linctus has been digested, eating ṣaṣṭika rice with milk is recommended.

children.text: vaikhānasādayo brahmaṇā nirmitametadupayujya rasāyanaṃ tandrādivarjitā medhādiyutā amitajīvitāścābhūvan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaikhānasa</s>s and others, using this <s>rasāyana</s> created by <s>Brahmā</s>, became free from drowsiness and the like, endowed with intelligence and the rest, and possessed of immeasurable life.
'Wealth-giving' means beneficial for wealth.

children.text: nanu rasāyanasya dhanārjanopāyatvābhāvāt kathaṃ dhanyatvam atra brūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But since <s>rasāyana</s> is not a means for acquiring wealth, how do we call it wealth-giving here?
It is so because the effect is figuratively applied to the cause.

children.text: tathā hi rasāyanamidam āmayaghnatvādārogye ca sati medhāsmṛtyādiyuktasya dhanāyodyamaṃ kurvato'vaśyaṃ dhanasampattiriti yuktameva ||
children.translated_text: For thus, since this <s>rasāyana</s> destroys disease, and when health exists, a person endowed with intelligence, memory, and the like, making effort for wealth, necessarily obtains wealth; therefore it is quite proper.
But since the intended meaning is already stated by 'free from disease,' the mention of drowsiness and the like is surely unnecessary.
To this we reply:
By 'free from disease' the author of the treatise stated the capacity of this <s>rasāyana</s> to maintain health.
And the mention of drowsiness and the like is for the purpose of showing that it is especially superior even in the destruction of disease.
In a decoction of <s>pañcamūla</s> consisting of <s>abhayā</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, and fivefold roots,
one should cook it in the juice of creepers and <s>palāśa</s>, twice as much, and in milk, eight times as much.

children.text: ghṛtasya kumbhaṃ madhukaṃ madhūkaṃ kākoliyugmaṃ ca balāṃ svaguptām ||
children.translated_text: A jar of ghee, <s>madhuka</s>, <s>madhūka</s>, the pair of <s>kākolī</s>s, <s>balā</s>, and <s>svaguptā</s>,

children.text: sakṣīraśuklām ṛṣabhaṃ sajīvaṃ sukhāmbupas tacca pibed guṇāḍhyam ||
children.translated_text: together with milky <s>śuklā</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, and <s>jīva</s>; one should drink that, rich in virtues, after taking pleasant water.

children.text: abhayāmalakānāṃ sahasraṃ dṛḍhaṃ kaṇāsahasrānvitam ajīrṇapalāśakṣāradravīkṛtaṃ bhājane sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: One should place in a vessel one thousand <s>abhayā</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, firm ones, combined with one thousand <s>kaṇā</s>s, liquefied by the alkali of undigested <s>palāśa</s>.

children.text: kṣāre copayukte sati chāyāyāṃ śuṣkaṃ cūrṇitaṃ ca śarkarāyāścaturthāṃśena caturguṇābhyāṃ ghṛtamākṣikābhyāṃ yojyam ||
children.translated_text: When the alkali has been applied, it should be dried in the shade, powdered, and combined with one fourth part of sugar and with four times as much ghee and honey.

children.text: etad ghṛtakumbhe nidhāya bhūmau ṣaṇmāsasthitaṃ samuddhṛtya pūrvāhṇe yathāgni bhuktvā sātmyāhāraḥ sadā syāt ||
children.translated_text: Having placed this in a jar of ghee and kept it in the ground for six months, one should take it out and eat it in the forenoon according to digestive fire; he should always use a suitable diet.
Three āryā verses.

children.text: evametat sarvam upayujya saṃvatsaraśataṃ nīrogo jarārahito jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Having used all this in this way, one lives for a hundred years, free from disease and free from old age.
Especially, he is endowed with strength and the like.
The meter is <s>gīti-āryā</s>.

children.text: nīrujo jantvādibhir anupadruto yaḥ palāśastasya śirasi chinne 'ntardvihastamātraṃ tatkṣataṃ suṣirīkṛtaṃ gambhīraṃ navairāmalakaiḥ pūraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: A <s>palāśa</s> tree that is free from disease and not harmed by creatures and the like: when its top has been cut off, the wound inside, about two hastas in depth, should be hollowed out and made deep, and filled with fresh <s>āmalaka</s> fruits.

children.text: pūrṇaṃ yāvaddarbhairveṣṭitaṃ padminīkardamena lepitaṃ tata āraṇyair gomayair ādīpya nivāte svedayet ||
children.translated_text: When it is full, it should be wrapped with darbha grass, smeared with lotus mud, then ignited with forest cow-dung and steamed in a windless place.

children.text: tāni cāmalakāni svinnāni kṣaudraghṛtayutāni tṛptyā puruṣaḥ khādet
children.translated_text: A man should eat those steamed <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, mixed with honey and ghee, until satisfied.
Afterwards he should drink much boiled milk.
And with that same milk alone he should live for one month.
The meter is <s>indravajrā</s>.

children.text: rasāyanavidhau yānyuktāni kṣārādīni varjyāni tāni parihartavyāni yatnena ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure, those things beginning with alkalis that are said to be avoided should be carefully shunned.
Cold water should not be touched even with the hand.

children.text: tato'sya rasāyanavidhātur ekādaśe 'hni vyatikrānte keśādayaḥ patanti ||
children.translated_text: Then, for this practitioner of the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure, when the eleventh day has passed, the hair and the rest fall out.

children.text: tato'lpakaireva dinai rūpavāṃstaruṇīviṣaya akṣayaśaktigajasamānasāmarthya utkṛṣṭamedhādir asau bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then, within only a few days, he becomes handsome, youthful in relation to women, possessed of unfailing power, equal in capacity to an elephant, and endowed with excellent intelligence and the rest.
And he lives for a thousand years.
In the <s>upajāti</s> meter.

children.text: daśamūlādikaṃ palonmitam aikadhyaṃ toyadroṇa āmalakaśatāni pañca pacet ||
children.translated_text: One should cook together <s>daśamūla</s> and the other ingredients, measured by pala, in one droṇa of water, along with five hundred <s>āmalaka</s> fruits.

children.text: tasmāccaturthāṃśaṃ rasaṃ vigatāsthīni cāmalakāny ādāya tailaghṛtayoḥ pratyekaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ palair bharjayet ||
children.translated_text: From that, one should take a quarter part of the decoction and the <s>āmalaka</s> fruits with their stones removed, and fry them with twelve palas each of oil and ghee.
Joined with half a tulā of sugar, one should cook all this like a linctus.

children.text: snehasyārdhaṃ pakve śīte madhu tathā tavakṣīrīcatuṣpalaṃ kaṇādvipalaṃ kaṇārdhena caturjātaṃ ca dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: When half of the unctuous substance has been cooked away and it has cooled, one should add honey, four palas of <s>tavakṣīrī</s>, two palas of <s>kaṇā</s>, and, in half the amount of <s>kaṇā</s>, the four aromatics.

children.text: ato lehāt mātrāṃ kuṭīsthitaḥ pathyānyaśnann avalehayet ||
children.translated_text: From this linctus one should lick off a dose while staying in a hut and eating wholesome foods.

children.text: ity evaṃ prakāraḥ ayaṃ cyavanaprāśākhyo lehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the type of linctus called <s>Cyavanaprāśa</s>.

children.text: yaṃ lehaṃ prāśya cyavanasaṃjño munirjarākrānto'pi taruṇīlocanarañjana āsīt ||
children.translated_text: After taking this linctus, the sage named <s>Cyavana</s>, though overcome by old age, became pleasing to the eyes of young women.
This linctus removes cough and the other disorders.

children.text: upasargād asyatyūhyor vā vacanam iti taṅ ||
children.translated_text: Because of the rule, 'after a preverb, in asyati and ūhyati,' the ātmanepada ending is used.
For children and others it causes growth of the limbs.
And, when used according to the method stated for rasāyana, it produces intelligence and the other benefits.
The meter is <s>indravajrā</s>.

children.text: madhukena samā tulyā yuktā triphalā tathā samaiḥ sarvaiḥ yuktā upayuktā rasāyanaṃ sarvarogaghnī medhādidā ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Triphala</s>, equal and similar to <s>madhuka</s>, and joined with all the ingredients in equal parts, when used, becomes a rasāyana that destroys all diseases and gives intelligence and the like.
The rasāyanas consisting of <s>tavakṣīrī</s> and the others, each in turn, are to be explained as members of the <s>triphala</s> group.

children.text: sindhujanmanā saindhavena lohāḥ rūpyaṃ tāmraṃ sīsaṃ trapu aya iti pañca taiḥ suvarṇena ca pṛthagyuktā varā rasāyanamiti yojyam ||
children.translated_text: With what is born from the ocean, that is, rock salt, and separately joined with the metals, namely silver, copper, lead, tin, and iron, the five, and also with gold, the excellent preparation should be construed as a rasāyana.

children.text: madhusarpiṣetyekavacananirdeśād dvābhyāmapi yugapadyoga ekaṃ rasāyanaṃ vedyam ||
children.translated_text: Because of the singular expression 'with honey and ghee,' the combination with both together is to be understood as one rasāyana.
One should use the fresh juice of <s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> with regard to the strength of the digestive fire.
One should take powdered <s>madhuyaṣṭī</s> with milk.
Likewise one should use the juice of <s>guḍūcī</s>.

children.text: tathā saha mūlapuṣpābhyāṃ vartate sahamūlapuṣpī tasyāḥ śaṅkhapuṣpyāśca kalkaṃ prayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, since it exists together with root and flower, it is called <s>sahamūlapuṣpī</s>; one should use a paste of that and of <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>.

children.text: ityetāni rasāyanānyāyuṣpradāni rogaghnāni balādivardhanāni medhāyai hitāni ca ||
children.translated_text: These rasāyanas give life span, destroy disease, increase strength and the other qualities, and are beneficial for intelligence.
<s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> is especially intellect-promoting.
In the <s>upajāti</s> meter.

children.text: naladādibhiḥ supiṣṭaiḥ sāmānyaparibhāṣoktapramāṇāt triguṇena śaṅkhapuṣpīrasena ghṛtasyāḍhakaṃ kṣīrasahitaṃ vipakvaṃ prāśya jaḍo'pi naro vāgmī śrutadharaḥ sapratibho nirāmayaśca syāt ||
children.translated_text: After taking an āḍhaka of ghee cooked with milk and with the well-ground ingredients beginning with <s>nalada</s>, using three times the amount of <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> juice stated in the general rule, even a dull man becomes eloquent, retentive of what he has heard, quick-witted, and free from disease.
In the <s>aupacchandasika</s> meter.

children.text: mṛṇālādibhiḥ kalkaiḥ suvarṇaśakalānvitaṃ haiyaṃgavīnaṃ sakṣīraṃ pakvaṃ pañcāravindam iti pañcāravindāni yasminniti samāsaḥ evamagre'pi kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Butter freshly taken from curds, cooked with milk, with pastes beginning with lotus-fiber and containing flakes of gold, is called <s>pañcāravinda</s>; the compound means 'that in which there are five lotuses.' The same construction should also be made below.

children.text: etadghṛtaṃ naṣṭaśukrādibhir niṣevitavyam etanniṣevaṇe naitāni syur ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This ghee should be used by those whose semen has been lost and so on; the meaning is that, when this is used, these conditions will not occur.

children.text: yadghṛtaṃ nīlotpalasya nālādimat kāñcanaśakalānvitaṃ sakṣīraṃ vipakvaṃ tadapi catuṣkuvalayaṃ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: That ghee which is cooked with milk, containing the stalk and other parts of blue lotus and containing flakes of gold, is also well known as <s>catuṣkuvalaya</s>.
This is intellect-promoting even for cows and even for dull creatures.
How much more, then, for human beings?
The meaning is: especially for them, who possess intelligence.
In the <s>vasantatilakā</s> meter.
<s>Brāhmī</s> and the others should each be in the measure of three barley grains.
<s>Matsyākṣaka</s> is <s>pattūra</s>.
For gold, two barley grains.
For poison, one sesame seed.
And for ghee, one pala.
One should combine this all together.

children.text: jīrṇe cāsmin bheṣaje bahughṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ samākṣikaṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: When this medicine has been digested, one should prescribe a meal rich in ghee and mixed with honey.
By practicing this for a year, one becomes endowed with great intellect and the other qualities.
In the <s>upajāti-svāgatā</s> meter.
Free from old age and the like, and endowed with full prosperity and the other qualities, he lives for a hundred years.
In particular, skin diseases and the like are pacified by this, as are very strong disorders of vāta.
<s>Upajāti</s>.
At the beginning of autumn and the like, under the lunar mansion <s>Puṣya</s>, one should dig up the root of <s>nāgabalā</s>.

children.text: tasmānmūlāc cūrṇitād akṣamātraṃ karṣamātraṃ dugdhena pibet mākṣikājyābhyāṃ vā lihyāt kṣīravartano 'nannāśī ||
children.translated_text: From that powdered root, one should drink a quantity of one akṣa, that is, one karṣa, with milk, or lick it with honey and ghee, living on milk and eating no grain-food.

children.text: evaṃ varṣaprayogeṇa balavān san varṣaśataṃ jīvet ||
children.translated_text: By using it thus for a year, being strong, one lives for a hundred years.

children.text: gokṣurakaḥ phalābhimukho mūlayutaś chāyāviśuṣkaḥ ślakṣṇacūrṇitaḥ svarasena subhāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gokṣuraka</s>, with the fruit facing downward and with its root, should be dried in the shade, finely powdered, and thoroughly impregnated with its own juice.

children.text: tasmād gokṣurakāt mātrāṃ prāsṛtikīṃ parāṃ yaḥ kṣīreṇa pibet pariṇate tasmin dugdhenaiva ca śālīn bhakṣayet sa puruṣaḥ palaśatadvayopayogāt śaktyādiguṇaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: A man who drinks from that <s>gokṣuraka</s> a supreme dose of one prasṛti with milk, and, when it has been digested, eats śāli rice with milk alone, after using two hundred palas, becomes endowed with strength and the other qualities.
In the <s>upajāti-indravajrā</s> meter.

children.text: vārāhyā vṛddhadārakasya mūlam atyārdraṃ dugdhena māsaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: One should drink for a month, with milk, the very fresh root of <s>vārāhī</s>, that is, <s>vṛddhadāraka</s>.
Even when it has been digested, he should drink milk and eat no grain-food.

children.text: aparaṃ ca māsaṃ kṣīrānnāśī san jarāṃ jayati ||
children.translated_text: For another month, living on milk and rice, he conquers old age.

children.text: tasyā varāhyā mūlaṃ ślakṣṇacūrṇaṃ vā svarasena suṣṭhu bhāvitaṃ ghṛtamākṣikāplutaṃ lihyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or one should lick the finely powdered root of that <s>vārāhī</s>, thoroughly impregnated with its own juice and soaked in ghee and honey.

children.text: tena vā mūlakalkena pakvaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibet pūrvaguṇam ||
children.translated_text: Or one should drink ghee cooked with that root-paste; it has the qualities stated before.

children.text: vidāryādīṃś ca pṛthak pṛthak tadvad vṛddhadārakavat sarpirdugdhayutān medhādyāvahān upayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: And one should use <s>vidārī</s> and the others, each separately, in the same way as <s>vṛddhadāraka</s>, together with ghee and milk, bringing intelligence and the other benefits.
Then, when used, they bestow firmness of age and the other benefits.

children.text: citrako yathāyogaṃ puṣpaiḥ pītaiḥ śuklaiḥ kṛṣṇaiś ca yathottaraṃ guṇavān veditavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s>, according to its proper application, should be understood as possessing qualities in ascending order when it has yellow, white, and black flowers.
And, when applied according to rule, it becomes a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative treatment).

children.text: tasmāccitrakān mūlaṃ chāyāśuṣkaṃ māsaṃ cūrṇīkṛtaṃ ghṛtena madhughṛtābhyāṃ vā lihyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should take the root of <s>citraka</s>, dried in the shade for a month and powdered, and lick it with ghee, or with honey and ghee.
Or, observing celibacy, one should drink it with milk.
Or, eating wholesome food, one should drink it with water.

children.text: sukhī medhāvān balavān ramaṇīyo vapuṣmān dīptāgniḥ samāḥ śataṃ jīvati ||
children.translated_text: He lives for a hundred years, happy, intelligent, strong, attractive, handsome, and with blazing digestive fire.

children.text: tailena līḍhaścitrako māsena dāruṇān vātān jayati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s>, licked with oil, conquers severe disorders of wind within a month.
Drunk with cow's urine, it destroys white leprosy and skin diseases.
Drunk with buttermilk, it conquers piles.

children.text: bhallātakāni suniṣpannāni grīṣme saṃgṛhya dhānyarāśau nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: One should gather well-ripened <s>bhallātaka</s> fruits in the hot season and place them in a heap of grain.

children.text: hemante madhurasnigdhaśītalaiḥ saṃskṛtaśarīras tānyaṣṭāv aṣṭaguṇe jale kvāthayet ||
children.translated_text: In winter, after the body has been prepared with sweet, unctuous, and cooling things, one should boil eight of them in eight times as much water.
One should drink that decoction, reduced to one-eighth, cooled, and mixed with milk.

children.text: paścāttasmin pratidinaṃ caikaikaṃ bhallātakaṃ vardhayet adhikīkṛtya kvāthayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, in that preparation, one should increase by one <s>bhallātaka</s> each day; the meaning is that one should boil it after increasing the amount.
This is to continue for three periods of seven nights.

children.text: saptarātratrayāt paratas trīṇi trīṇyaruṣkarāṇi catvāriṃśataṃ yāvad vardhayet ||
children.translated_text: After the three seven-night periods, one should increase by threes, three <s>aruṣkara</s> fruits at a time, up to forty.
After that, one should reduce those <s>aruṣkara</s> fruits in the same way as they were increased.
Thus, over seven weeks, one should consume a thousand.
The man should keep himself restrained and eat ghee, milk, and sixty-day rice.

children.text: tathaiva ca bhallātakaprayogānta ekaviṃśatisaptāhān ghṛtakṣīraśāliṣaṣṭikabhojanaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the end of the <s>bhallātaka</s> regimen, for twenty-one weeks he should eat ghee, milk, and sixty-day rice.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtabhallātakaprayogo'pūrvā abhilaṣitā dayitāḥ āśiṣo labhate tathā viśeṣeṇa vahnipāṭavam ||
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the <s>bhallātaka</s> regimen, he obtains unprecedented beloved blessings that he has desired, and in particular keen digestive fire.
And he becomes free from diabetes and the like.

children.text: piṣṭaṃ śālicūrṇaṃ svedyate 'sminn iti piṣṭasvedanaṃ bhāṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: A vessel in which ground rice flour is steamed is called a <s>piṣṭasvedana</s> vessel.

children.text: tadarujair dṛḍhaiḥ bhallātakaistathā vijarjaritaiḥ pūrṇaṃ sat kṛtacchidraṃ bhūminikhāte kumbhe pratiṣṭhitaṃ kṛṣṇamṛttikayā liptamanantaraṃ gomayāgninā mṛdunā parivāritaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: When that vessel is filled with painless, firm <s>bhallātaka</s> fruits, broken up in that way, perforated, set over a pot sunk into the ground, smeared with black clay, and then surrounded with a mild fire of cow-dung fuel, one should cook it.

children.text: tatsvaraso yastatra dharānikhāte kumbhe patet tam anyasminn ahani gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: The expressed juice from it that falls there into the pot sunk in the earth should be collected on another day.

children.text: amuṃ pūrvoktaṃ svarasaṃ mākṣikāṣṭamabhāgaṃ dviguṇaghṛtaṃ pūrvavidhinā yantritātmā sann upayujya tānevapūrvoktān guṇān prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Using this previously mentioned expressed juice, together with one-eighth part honey and twice as much ghee, according to the previously stated rule and with the self restrained, one obtains those same qualities mentioned above.
There are three <s>āryā</s> verses, with the middle one slightly rapid in its opening.

children.text: suniṣpannāni bhallātakāni pākena paricyutānyāḍhakasaṃmitāni iṣṭikācūrṇakaṇair ghṛṣṭāni jalena prakṣālya mārutena saṃśoṣya na tv ātape tato jarjarāṇi jaladroṇe vipacet ||
children.translated_text: Well-ripened <s>bhallātaka</s> fruits, separated by cooking and measuring one <s>āḍhaka</s>, should be rubbed with particles of powdered brick, washed with water, dried by wind and not in the sun, then crushed and cooked in a <s>droṇa</s> of water.

children.text: pādaśeṣadhṛtagālitaṃ śītaṃ ca tadrasaṃ punarapi kṣīradroṇasahitaṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: When one quarter remains, it should be strained through cloth and cooled; then that juice should again be cooked together with a <s>droṇa</s> of milk.

children.text: tasmin pādaśeṣasthe tulyapramāṇaṃ sarpiḥ pakvaṃ śarkarācūrṇena yutaṃ yathecchaṃ prakṛtyādivaśād yuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: When one quarter remains in that, ghee of equal measure is to be cooked with it, mixed with powdered sugar, and used as desired according to constitution and the like.

children.text: tacca khajaloḍanenaikībhūtaṃ dhānyamadhye saptarātraṃ suguptaṃ sthāpyam ||
children.translated_text: And, when it has been made homogeneous by stirring with a churn-stick, it should be kept well concealed within grain for seven nights.
The metres are <s>indravajrā</s>, <s>svāgatā</s>, and <s>śālinī</s>.

children.text: tamamṛtarasatulyapākaṃ yaḥ pūrvāhṇe prāśaṃ lehaṃ bhakṣayan paścādyatheṣṭaṃ jalaṃ kṣīraṃ māṃsarasaṃ vā pibati sa smṛtyādiyutaḥ suvarṇaughagauro dīrghamāyuḥ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats in the forenoon that linctus, cooked to be like the nectar of immortality, and afterwards drinks water, milk, or meat broth as desired, obtains long life, endowed with memory and the rest, and with a complexion bright as a mass of gold.
The metre is <s>mālinī</s>.

children.text: jaladroṇe vraṇakṛtāṃ bhallātakānāṃ śatatrayādvipakvāt kvāthasyāḍhake 'vaśiṣṭe tilatailāḍhakaṃ tiktādibhiḥ pālikaiḥ kalkitaiḥ pakvaṃ niḥśeṣakuṣṭhaniṣūdanāya paraṃ śreṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: From three hundred wounded <s>bhallātaka</s> fruits cooked in a <s>droṇa</s> of water, when one <s>āḍhaka</s> of decoction remains, an <s>āḍhaka</s> of sesame oil cooked with one-pala pastes of the bitter group and the like is supremely excellent for utterly destroying skin diseases.
The metre is <s>vasantatilakā</s>.

children.text: āmalakatvagādibhir ekādaśabhiḥ saha pratyekaṃ bhallātakam upayuktaṃ praśastaśarīrakaraṇakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: A single <s>bhallātaka</s> used together with each of the eleven substances beginning with <s>āmalaka</s> bark is a cause of producing an excellent body.

children.text: tathā param atiśayena medhyam āyuṣpradaṃ ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, it is in the highest degree intellect-promoting and life-giving.
The metre is <s>pṛthvī</s>.

children.text: bhallātakāni tīkṣṇāni suniṣpannāni dahanatulyāni tāni yathāvidhi prayuktānyamṛtatulyāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhallātaka</s> fruits are sharp, well-ripened, and like fire; when applied according to rule, they become like nectar.

children.text: śleṣmottho rogaḥ sa nāsti vibandhaś ca sa kaścid api na vidyate yaṃ rogaṃ vibandhaṃ vā bhallātakaṃ drutataraṃ paṭutaradahanakaraṃ na hanyāt ||
children.translated_text: There is no disease arising from phlegm, nor any obstruction whatsoever, which disease or obstruction <s>bhallātaka</s>, acting very swiftly and producing a very sharp fire, does not destroy.

children.text: vātātapavidhāv api bhallātakasya kulatthādīni viśeṣeṇa varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Even in the regimen concerning wind and sun, one should especially avoid horse-gram and the like when using <s>bhallātaka</s>.
The trees known as <s>tuvara</s> are <s>tubaraka</s> trees, grown on the shore of the western ocean.
By the qualifier beginning with 'wave,' he indicates that they are very near the ocean.

children.text: tebhyo vṛkṣebhyo jaladāgame supakvāni phalāni gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: From those trees one should take fully ripe fruits at the coming of the rainy season.

children.text: phalebhyo'pi majjño gṛhītvā śoṣayitvā suṣṭhu cūrṇayitvā ca tilavad droṇyāṃ pīḍayet ||
children.translated_text: From the fruits also, after taking the kernels, drying them, and powdering them well, one should press them in a trough as one presses sesame.
Or one should boil them like safflower.

children.text: tacca tailaṃ siddhaṃ punaḥ pacettoyakṣayaṃ yāvat ||
children.translated_text: That oil, once prepared, should again be cooked until the water is exhausted.
When cooked, it should be taken down and placed in a heap of dry cow-dung for half a month.

children.text: yantrapīḍitaṃ tu prakṛtyaiva nistoyaṃ tailaṃ tad akvathitam eva nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: But oil pressed by a machine is naturally without water; therefore it should be stored without being boiled.

children.text: tataḥ pakṣād anantaraṃ tailamuddhṛtya snigdhasvinno hṛtadoṣo mantreṇānena majjasāretyādinā pavitritasya tailasya śubhadivase caturthena bhaktenāntarito 'harmukhe karṣaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after a fortnight, having taken out the oil, when he has been oleated and sweated and his doṣas have been removed, at the beginning of the day, after an interval of four meals, on an auspicious day, he should drink one karṣa of the oil that has been purified by the mantra beginning with 'majjasāra'.

children.text: tena tailenāsya puṃsa ūrdhvam adhaśca punaḥ punar doṣā yānti ||
children.translated_text: By means of that oil, this man's doṣas repeatedly pass out upward and downward.
Afterwards, in the afternoon, he should drink cool gruel without oil and salt.

children.text: ittham anena prakāreṇa parihāryān pariharan pañca divasāni tailaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, avoiding the things to be avoided, he should drink the oil for five days.
Eating rice with mung-bean soup for a fortnight, he is freed from all skin diseases.

children.text: tad eva tuvarāsthitailaṃ khadirakvāthena triguṇena samyak pakvaṃ pūrvavatkarīṣe pakṣaṃ nihitaṃ māsaṃ suyantritaḥ pibet ||
children.translated_text: That same oil from <s>tuvarā</s> kernels, properly cooked with three times as much decoction of <s>khadira</s>, placed as before in cow-dung for a fortnight, should be drunk for a month by one who is well restrained.

children.text: tena ca tailenābhyaktaśarīro bhojanaṃ pūrvoktaṃ mudgarasānnaṃ vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: And with that oil his body should be anointed, and he should take the previously stated food, rice with mung-bean soup.

children.text: etena prayogeṇa śīghraṃ kuṣṭhavantaṃ puruṣam upakramet ||
children.translated_text: By this treatment one should quickly treat a man afflicted with skin disease.

children.text: tad eva tuvarāsthitailaṃ khadiram antareṇa ghṛtamadhuyutaṃ pakṣaṃ pītaṃ san māṃsarasāhāraṃ naraṃ dviśatāyuṣam vidhatte ||
children.translated_text: That same oil from <s>tuvarā</s> kernels, without <s>khadira</s>, mixed with ghee and honey, when drunk for a fortnight, makes a man who lives on meat broth live for two hundred years.

children.text: tad eva tailaṃ nasye pañcāśadvāsarān sevitaṃ varaśarīraṃ śrutadharaṃ trivarṣaśatāyuṣaṃ puruṣam karoti ||
children.translated_text: That same oil, used as a nasal medication for fifty days, makes a man possess an excellent body, retain what he has heard, and live for three hundred years.

children.text: pañca pippalīr athavā saptāṣṭau vā daśa vā mākṣikasarpirbhyāṃ rasāyanaguṇam abhilaṣya varṣam ekaṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Desiring the qualities of a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative treatment), one should use five <s>pippalī</s> fruits, or seven, eight, or ten, with honey and ghee for one year.

children.text: palāśakṣārabhāvitāḥ pippalyaḥ sarpiṣā bharjitā mākṣikānvitās tisraḥ pūrvāhṇe tisro bhuktvā tisro bhojanāgre prayojyāḥ rasāyanaguṇaṃ kāmayamānena ||
children.translated_text: Three <s>pippalī</s> fruits steeped in alkali of <s>palāśa</s>, fried in ghee, and mixed with honey should be taken in the forenoon, three after eating, and three before the meal by one who desires the quality of a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: daśa dināni daśapaippalikaṃ dinaṃ kramavṛddhyā kṣīreṇa saha yojayet vardhamānā daśa pippalīḥ prayojayed ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For ten days one should take a day consisting of ten <s>pippalī</s> fruits together with milk, increasing in sequence; the meaning is that one should take an increasing course of ten <s>pippalī</s> fruits.
In the same way, one should reduce the ten-<s>pippalī</s> day together with milk.
When the medicine has been digested, he should eat sixty-day rice with milk and ghee.

children.text: ayam evaṃprakāraḥ sahasrapippalīnāṃ prayogo rasāyanaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: This procedure of this kind, involving a thousand <s>pippalī</s> fruits, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: tāḥ pippalyaḥ piṣṭāḥ satyo balavadbhir naraiḥ pātavyāḥ madhyabalairnaraiḥ kvathitāḥ peyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>pippalī</s> fruits, when ground, should be drunk by strong men; by men of middling strength they should be drunk after being decocted.

children.text: tadvacceti anenaiva krameṇa chāgakṣīreṇa saha dve sahasre prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: And similarly: by this same sequence one should use two thousand together with goat's milk.

children.text: ebhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ prayogaiḥ pippalya upayuktāḥ kāsādīñśophādīṃś ca jayanti ||
children.translated_text: When used by these previously mentioned procedures, <s>pippalī</s> fruits conquer cough and the other disorders, and swellings and the other disorders.
At night one should smear an iron vessel with merely two karṣas of <s>pippalī</s>.

children.text: tacca jalāñjaliyugena prātaḥ pibet saṃvatsaraṃ svecchābhojanapānakriyaḥ etacca rasāyanaṃ pūrvaguṇam ||
children.translated_text: In the morning he should drink that with two handfuls of water for a year, while following his desired practice of eating and drinking; and this <s>rasāyana</s> has the qualities stated before.
The metre is <s>indravajrā</s>.

children.text: śuṇṭhyādīn pṛthageva pippalīr iva lohopaliptān upayujya varṣaśataṃ rogajarārahito jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Using ginger and the other substances separately, just like <s>pippalī</s>, after they have been smeared on iron, he lives a hundred years free from disease and old age.

children.text: amūni pūrvoktāni rasāyanāni lohalepanāni kṣīrāñjalibhyāṃ dugdhapalāṣṭakena upayuktāni pūrvoktaguṇātiśayam āyuḥprakarṣaṃ ca tato dviguṇaṃ vidadhati ||
children.translated_text: These previously mentioned <s>rasāyana</s> preparations, the iron-smearing ones, when used with handfuls of milk, or with eight palas of milk, produce a superiority over the previously stated qualities and an increase of life twice as great as that.
At the beginning and end the metre is called <s>indravajrā</s>, while the middle one is <s>upajāti</s>.

children.text: asanādikvāthena bhāvitāṃ vākucīṃ mākṣikādibhir yuktāṃ varṣam avalihan pāriṇāmān vayaḥpariṇatijān vikārān jahāti ||
children.translated_text: By licking <s>vākucī</s> steeped in a decoction of <s>asana</s> and the other drugs, and combined with honey and the like, for a year, one abandons disorders of maturation, those born from the transformation of age.
Likewise, while eating wholesome and measured food, one abandons disorders born from diet.
The metre is <s>mālinī</s>.

children.text: dāruṇena kuṣṭhena vyāptadeho yaḥ śaśāṅkalekhāṃ kṛṣṇatilayutāṃ niyamena vatsaraṃ bhakṣayet sa candrakāntiṃ śarīreṇa jayet ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, his body pervaded by severe skin disease, regularly eats <s>śaśāṅkalekhā</s> together with black sesame for a year conquers the moon's radiance with his body.
The metre is <s>upajāti</s>.

children.text: ye puruṣā vituṣīkṛtāyā indurājyāścūrṇair yuktāt kṣīrāt sujātāt sāraṃ navanītākhyam uddhṛtya mākṣikeṇa saha lihanti paścāt tadeva takraṃ ca ye pibanti te kuṣṭhavantaḥ śīryamāṇaśarīrāḥ samudbhūtāṅgulighrāṇāḥ śobhante ||
children.translated_text: Those men with skin disease, whose bodies are wasting away and whose fingers and noses have grown back, who lick with honey the excellent butter called <s>navanīta</s>, extracted from well-produced milk mixed with powders of husked <s>indurājī</s>, and who afterwards drink that very buttermilk, become splendid.
They are like trees that have again produced fresh young shoots.
The metre is <s>indravajrā</s>.

children.text: svarbhānor amṛtāpaharaṇāparādhena kaṇṭhācchinnādye 'mṛtasya bindavo dharitryāṃ patitās te laśunatvaṃ prāptāḥ yato 'smāddhetor daityadehotthaṃ laśunam ato dvijā na bhakṣayanti sākṣāccāmṛtasambhūtatvāddhetor asau rasono rasāyanaṃ grāmaṇīḥ śreṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of <s>Svarbhānu</s>'s offense of stealing the nectar of immortality, when he was cut from the neck, drops of nectar fell onto the earth and became garlic. Since garlic arose from a demon's body for this reason, twice-born men do not eat it; yet because it was directly born from nectar, this <s>rasona</s> is the foremost, the best, among <s>rasāyana</s> substances.
In the cold season, in winter and the dewy season, one should practice the use of garlic.
When phlegm is excessive, one should practice it even in spring.
When wind is predominant, one should practice it even in the rainy season.
Or one afflicted by wind should practice it at all times by following the regimen of the hot season.

children.text: kīdṛśaḥ san snigdhā śuddhā ca tanur yasya sa evam ||
children.translated_text: In what condition? When his body is oleated and purified, such is the condition.

children.text: tathā śītalairmadhuraiścopaskṛtaḥ saṃskṛtaḥ āśayo yasya sa evam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when his digestive tract has been prepared and refined with cooling and sweet things, such is the condition.

children.text: tathā tasya laśunasya śekharakarṇapūrābhyāṃ maṇḍitā anucarāḥ sevakāḥ aṅgaṇe yasya sa tathā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when his attendants, his servants, are adorned with crests and ear-fillings made of that garlic in his courtyard, such is the condition.

children.text: tasya laśunasya kandān vasantaṛtujāṃs tathā himavaddeśajāṃś śakadeśajān vā uddhṛtatvaco rātrau madirābījapūrarasādibhis timayet kledayet ||
children.translated_text: He should take bulbs of that garlic, grown in the spring season and likewise from the Himalayan region or from the Śaka country, remove their skins, and at night moisten and soak them with liquor, citron juice, and the like.

children.text: tatkalkasya svarasaṃ dhautavastrapīḍitaṃ madirāyāḥ surūḍhāyās tribhāgena yutaṃ madyāder vā tribhāgena yutam athavā tasminneva kāle surādibhir yutaṃ mātrayā deśakālāturādyapekṣiṇyā ālocya nirūpya tailādibhir vā pṛthagyuktaṃ yadi vā kvāthena yathā vyādhivaśād yuktaṃ kevalameva vā rasaṃ prākpūrvaṃ gaṇḍūṣamātraṃ pibed galanāḍīviśodhanāya ||
children.translated_text: The fresh juice of that garlic paste, pressed through a washed cloth, mixed with one third part of well-fermented wine, or mixed with one third part of liquor and the like, or else at that very time mixed with surā and similar drinks, in a dose that depends on place, time, the patient, and so forth, after considering and determining it, or separately combined with oils and the like, or, if appropriate, combined with a decoction according to the force of the disease, or even the juice alone, should first be drunk in a quantity fit for a gargle, for the purification of the throat channel.
When there is pain, constant fomentation is best.
